items.detail: The **Nasdaq** jumped 1.19% to 27,190.86 on Friday and the S&P 500 gained about 0.7% to 7,722.72, after the September jobs report came in far weaker than expected.
items.why: Only 29,000 jobs were added against roughly 84,000 expected, so traders scaled back bets on another Fed hike.

items.detail: Odds of a Fed hike on October 28 fell to the **mid-teens**, down from about one in four before the data, as unemployment rose to 4.2%.
items.why: Downward revisions to earlier months and weak 0.1% wage growth point to a cooling job market.

items.detail: The dollar had its **worst day in a month** after payrolls, but the MSCI EM index still closed Friday 0.10% lower because Asia traded before the data.
items.why: A softer dollar after the jobs miss helps EM currencies and makes their assets cheaper for foreign buyers.

items.detail: India reopens Monday with the **Nifty 50** on a four-day losing streak, and the RBI's October 7 decision is the week's big event.
items.why: Foreign funds pulled over ₹26,000 crore in three sessions, but weaker US jobs data may ease the pressure.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** rose 0.94% to 2,832.90 on Friday, a second straight gain that extends its rebound from a weak September.
items.why: Lower odds of a Fed hike ease borrowing costs, which matters most for smaller, debt-heavy companies.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** traded around **$84,600** early Saturday, after topping $85,000 on Friday for the first time in the current range.
items.why: Bitcoin ETFs swung back to $170 million of inflows on October 1, and short sellers closing out bets added to the move.

items.detail: **Ether** slipped to about **$2,690**, giving back Friday's small gain and staying below $2,800.
items.why: The jobs miss lifted risk appetite, but ether lagged bitcoin and buyers didn't push it toward its ceiling.

items.detail: **Solana** climbed back above $120 to about **$122** on Friday, up roughly 3% in 24 hours.
items.why: A $7.7 million wave of forced short liquidations and record weekly Solana ETF inflows pushed it higher.

items.detail: **Spot gold** rose nearly 1% to around **$4,217** on Friday, bouncing back toward $4,200 after the US jobs report.
items.why: The payrolls miss cut Fed hike odds and weakened the dollar, both good for a metal that pays no interest.

crossCuttingTheme: September's weak jobs report, just 29,000 added, cut the odds of an October Fed hike and pushed the dollar to its worst day in a month, lifting tech stocks, small caps, gold and bitcoin together.
